chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Harun from Murram from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'When should I perform the night prayer?' He said, 'Perform it at the end of the night.' I said, 'But I do not wake up (fully).' He said, 'Wake up once, perform it, then sleep and make it up later. When you are eager to make it up during the day, you will wake up (fully).'
ai.seo_question: How to perform the night prayer if you are not fully awake?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises performing the night prayer at the end of the night, offering a pragmatic solution for those who struggle with waking: perform it upon waking, then sleep, allowing the natural desire to make it up during the day to ensure proper awakening. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual discipline with human physiological realities, ensuring consistency in worship rather than perfectionism that leads to abandonment. It reflects the principle of *taysir* (easing) in ritual practice, encouraging sustained devotion through manageable routines.
